# dorbdb5

> Orthogonalize a column vector against the columns of an orthonormal-column matrix; if the projection collapses, return a deterministic vector from the orthogonal complement.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dorbdb5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorbdb5';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dorbdb5(
    order,
    m1, m2, N,
    X1, strideX1,
    X2, strideX2,
    Q1, LDQ1,
    Q2, LDQ2,
    WORK
) → integer
```

Orthogonalizes the column vector `X = [X1; X2]` against the columns of `Q = [Q1; Q2]`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `m1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of `X1` and rows of `Q1`<br>Requires `m1 ≥ 0` |
| `m2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of `X2` and rows of `Q2`<br>Requires `m2 ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns in `Q1` and `Q2`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `X1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length m1</sub> | **in/out** · Top part of the vector |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | `X1` stride length |
| `X2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length m2</sub> | **in/out** · Bottom part of the vector |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | `X2` stride length |
| `Q1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>m1 × N</sub> | Top part of the orthonormal basis matrix |
| ↳ `LDQ1` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q1`<br>Column-major requires `LDQ1 ≥ max(1, m1)`<br>Row-major requires `LDQ1 ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `Q2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>m2 × N</sub> | Bottom part of the orthonormal basis matrix |
| ↳ `LDQ2` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q2`<br>Column-major requires `LDQ2 ≥ max(1, m2)`<br>Row-major requires `LDQ2 ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length at least `N`) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `m1`: The dimension of `X1` and the number of rows in `Q1`. $0 \le M_{1}$.
- `m2`: The dimension of `X2` and the number of rows in `Q2`. $0 \le M_{2}$.
- `N`: The number of columns in `Q1` and `Q2`. $0 \le N$.
- `X1`: On entry, the top part of the vector to be orthogonalized. On exit, the top part of the projected vector.
- `X2`: On entry, the bottom part of the vector to be orthogonalized. On exit, the bottom part of the projected vector.
- `Q1`: The top part of the orthonormal basis matrix.
- `Q2`: The bottom part of the orthonormal basis matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `info` (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `strideX1 < 1`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument is invalid (rejected when `strideX2 < 1`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, m1 )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, m2 )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` `m1` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `m2` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `strideX1` must be nonzero
- `RangeError` `strideX2` must be nonzero
- `RangeError` `LDQ1` must satisfy the leading-dimension constraint
- `RangeError` `LDQ2` must satisfy the leading-dimension constraint

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dorbdb5.strided(
    m1, m2, N,
    X1, strideX1, offsetX1,
    X2, strideX2, offsetX2,
    Q1, strideQ11, strideQ12, offsetQ1,
    Q2, strideQ21, strideQ22, offsetQ2,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Orthogonalizes the column vector `X = [X1; X2]` against the columns of `Q = [Q1; Q2]`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `m1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of `X1` and number of rows in `Q1`<br>Requires `m1 ≥ 0` |
| `m2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of `X2` and number of rows in `Q2`<br>Requires `m2 ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns in `Q1` and `Q2`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `X1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length m1</sub> | **in/out** · Top part of the vector |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | `X1` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetX1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X1` |
| `X2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length m2</sub> | **in/out** · Bottom part of the vector |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | `X2` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetX2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `X2` |
| `Q1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>m1 × N</sub> | Top part of the orthonormal basis matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ11` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Q1` |
| ↳ `strideQ12` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Q1` |
| ↳ `offsetQ1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Q1` |
| `Q2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>m2 × N</sub> | Bottom part of the orthonormal basis matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ21` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Q2` |
| ↳ `strideQ22` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Q2` |
| ↳ `offsetQ2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Q2` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length at least `N`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | `WORK` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `m1`: The dimension of `X1` and the number of rows in `Q1`. $0 \le M_{1}$.
- `m2`: The dimension of `X2` and the number of rows in `Q2`. $0 \le M_{2}$.
- `N`: The number of columns in `Q1` and `Q2`. $0 \le N$.
- `X1`: On entry, the top part of the vector to be orthogonalized. On exit, the top part of the projected vector.
- `X2`: On entry, the bottom part of the vector to be orthogonalized. On exit, the bottom part of the projected vector.
- `Q1`: The top part of the orthonormal basis matrix.
- `Q2`: The bottom part of the orthonormal basis matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `info` (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `strideX1 < 1`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument is invalid (rejected when `strideX2 < 1`)
- `RangeError` `m1` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `m2` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `strideX1` must be nonzero
- `RangeError` `strideX2` must be nonzero

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dorbdb5()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DORBDB5`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dorbdb5.f).
-   `dorbdb5` differs from `dorbdb6` in that, when the orthogonalization collapses to zero, `dorbdb5` searches the standard basis vectors `e_1, ..., e_(m1+m2)` (X1 partition first) and returns the first one that is orthogonal to range(Q).
-   `dorbdb5` is used as a kernel inside the LAPACK CS Decomposition (CSD) family of routines (notably `dorbdb1`-`dorbdb4`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dorbdb5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorbdb5';

// Construct an orthonormal basis Q whose two columns span (e1; e1)/sqrt(2) and (e2; e2)/sqrt(2), stored as 4-by-2 column-major matrices split into top (Q1) and bottom (Q2) halves of two rows each.
const sq2 = 1.0 / Math.sqrt( 2.0 );
const Q1 = new Float64Array( [ sq2, 0.0, 0.0, sq2 ] );
const Q2 = new Float64Array( [ sq2, 0.0, 0.0, sq2 ] );

// Vector to orthogonalize: X = (1, 2 | 3, 4)
const X1 = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const X2 = new Float64Array( [ 3.0, 4.0 ] );

// Workspace
const WORK = new Float64Array( 2 );

dorbdb5( 'column-major', 2, 2, 2, X1, 1, X2, 1, Q1, 2, Q2, 2, WORK );

console.log( 'X1 =', Array.prototype.slice.call( X1 ) );
console.log( 'X2 =', Array.prototype.slice.call( X2 ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORBDB5`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORBDB5 orthogonalizes the column vector

```text
     X = [ X1 ]
         [ X2 ]
with respect to the columns of
     Q = [ Q1 ] .
         [ Q2 ]
```

The columns of Q must be orthonormal.

If the projection is zero according to Kahan's "twice is enough" criterion, then some other vector from the orthogonal complement is returned. This vector is chosen in an arbitrary but deterministic way.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
